quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Move to the right side and stop.
Stop right where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear its siren, you must pull to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: What should you do first when parallel parking between two cars?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up next to the car in front of the parking space.
Back up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up next to the car in front of the parking space.
questions.explanation: After you find a parking space and check traffic, stop next to the car in front of the space. Then turn your wheels to park.

questions.question: What does an orange sign mean?

options.text: A no passing zone is starting.
A railroad crossing is ahead.
A school zone is ahead.
Construction work is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn about construction, maintenance, and emergency work ahead.

questions.question: When can you drive on the left side of the center line?

options.text: When passing another vehicle, if passing is allowed.
When you can see 500 feet ahead and behind.
When the shoulder is rough and the ditch is deep.
Any time no cars are coming toward you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When passing another vehicle, if passing is allowed.
questions.explanation: You can cross the center line to pass another vehicle only when passing is permitted. Never cross a solid yellow line or pass in a no passing zone.

questions.question: What should you do when you approach a railroad crossing?

options.text: Slow down.
Look for a train.
Be ready to stop.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If the red lights flash or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Never go around the gate.

questions.question: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Get out and walk for help.
Lie down and sleep in your car.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found there.
questions.explanation: If stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle. Walking in a snowstorm is unsafe.

questions.question: If a bus is signaling to return to the road after a stop, what must you do?

options.text: Honk to let them know you are there.
Move to the left lane.
Yield the right of way.
Speed up to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right of way.
questions.explanation: You must yield to a bus that is signaling to enter the road after picking up or dropping off passengers. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus merge safely.

questions.question: What does a painted arrow on the road mean?

options.text: Drivers in that lane may make that movement if they choose.
Drivers must make that movement only if traffic lights are broken.
Drivers must always stop before making that movement.
Drivers must make that movement while obeying traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must make that movement while obeying traffic signals.
questions.explanation: A painted arrow shows the direction drivers in that lane must go. Follow traffic signs and signals before moving in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: What should you do when you approach an accident scene?

options.text: Focus on your own driving.
Keep moving.
Stop if you are involved or if help has not arrived.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: Only stop at an accident scene if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Keep your attention on driving and watch for people near the road. Do not stop just to look.

questions.question: Can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, after the train passes.
No, never.
Yes, when the lights stop flashing.
Yes, when other drivers do.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: You must always stop at railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These include flashing red lights, a lowered gate, a flagman, or a train's horn. Never try to go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?

options.text: Service sign
Regulatory sign
Warning sign
Stop sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to hazards or special situations ahead.

questions.question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crashes?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Say no to drinks by telling people you are driving.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: To avoid alcohol-related crashes, decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol impairs your judgment, making it hard to make safe choices once you start drinking.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A left curve is ahead.
A series of curves is ahead.
An S-curve is ahead.
The road will be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will be slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes especially slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: What happens when you drive while distracted?

options.text: It is never dangerous.
You usually react slower to hazards.
You usually drive faster.
It is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You usually react slower to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions make drivers react more slowly to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, what must you do?

options.text: Keep your normal driving speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Yield to pedestrians.
Increase your driving speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: You may turn right on a green light unless a sign says otherwise. When turning, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A community group is picking up trash ahead.
Workers are on or very near the road in the work zone ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or very near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that workers may be on or near the roadway ahead. Drive carefully through work zones.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side as traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing the traffic coming toward them.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Human error
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or when drivers act unexpectedly. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: An oncoming car is to your left and a bicyclist is to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Go between both.
Let the car pass and then pass the bike.
Pass the bike quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass and then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: When you have multiple hazards, deal with one at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires help your vehicle grip slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter driving is difficult and requires extra care. Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels regularly. Snow tires improve traction on slippery roads.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with no gates or flashing lights, but with a standard crossbuck sign. What should you do?

options.text: Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn down your radio so you can hear if a train is approaching.
Continue only after a flagger clears you to proceed, if one is present.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, obey their instructions.

questions.question: What is the number one cause of deaths on Montana's roads?

options.text: Poor road conditions
Bad weather
Drunk drivers
Speeding

questions.correctAnswerText: Drunk drivers
questions.explanation: Drunk driving causes over 23,000 deaths yearly across the country. In Montana, alcohol is involved in 50 percent of all traffic deaths and over 2,100 injuries. Drunk drivers are the leading cause of fatal crashes on Montana's roads.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Maintain
Vary
Reduce

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce
questions.explanation: Slow down when turning. Go at a speed that lets you control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and respond to surprises.

questions.question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and a slash through the middle mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
An action is forbidden.
Some drivers must yield to other drivers.
Drivers must go below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is forbidden.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that forbid actions are rectangular, white, with red and black markings. A red circle and slash over a black symbol means that action is not allowed.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they:

options.text: Will drive the same as if they were thinking clearly.
Can drive faster because they are more alert.
Should calm down and focus before starting the engine.
Should call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should calm down and focus before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions like worry, anger, or sadness make it hard to drive well. Your mind focuses on the emotion instead of the road. Calm down and get focused before you drive.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:

options.text: Slows down your reactions.
Makes you feel less confident.
Metabolizes faster.
Reduces driving mistakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows down your reactions.
questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reactions, makes you feel overconfident, and causes you to make more mistakes.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Speed up to create more distance.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors several times each minute to spot tailgaters and fast-approaching cars. If a car is too close, slow down to let it pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because cars follow too closely.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from certain lanes. A green arrow means:

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
You can proceed, but you must turn in the direction the arrow shows.
You may proceed only if there is also a circular green light.
It points the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can proceed, but you must turn in the direction the arrow shows.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can proceed, but traffic in that lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: How alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment:

options.text: Is less serious with beer than wine.
Is less serious with wine than beer.
Is worse with hard ciders and mixed drinks.
Depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: Depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: All types of alcohol harm your reflexes and judgment. The type of drink does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream matters.

questions.question: You can safely pass on a two-way, two-lane street only if:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You can only pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street if you can see the road clearly ahead, you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle can go fast enough to pass. Do not pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway?

options.text: Yes, as long as you are not driving.
Yes, if you sit in the back seat.
Yes, if you sit in the back of a pickup truck.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have alcohol in a vehicle on a public road. You cannot have an open alcohol container in the driver or passenger area of any vehicle on a public road.

questions.question: What should you do if your gas pedal gets stuck while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your gas pedal sticks, keep looking at the road. Shift the car to neutral quickly and press the brake pedal hard. When it is safe, pull to the side of the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: The right lane ends and you must merge left.
The road curves ahead.
An intersection is coming up.
Road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and you must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the right lane is ending. All traffic in the right lane must move left.
